newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols edge up as bonds slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols edge up as bonds slide.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options edged up as underlying bond prices slid, traders said.

Still, a lack of important economic data in the first half of this week and perception that the bond market was still on a fairly stable uptrend after Friday's strong rally limited gains in volatilities, they added.

"Vols are really cheap to start with," said a a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. He added that volatilities often tended to be firm on Mondays as the market's weekend time-decay markdowns on Fridays sometimes overshot.

"Volatilities were actually up a little bit when we broke out of the range (to the upside) on Friday and then they settled back down," a brokerage trader at the CME said. "Now that the (futures) market has come back a little bit, it's helping volatilities come down."
Implied volatilities for September shed about 0.1 point to around 8.5 percent and December lost nearly 0.5 point to 10.5.

There were few large deals today, but an investment bank was said to have sold off a total of about 8,000 short-June 93.50 calls it had bought on Friday. Short Junes are options priced off June 1998 futures but which expire this month.
